arguments.decision: method/basis for H2 equilibrium bond length
arguments.recommendation: CCSD(T) / cc-pVTZ via psi4 (closed-shell singlet, charge 0, multiplicity 1)
arguments.reasoning: H2 is a 2-electron system, so CCSD(T) is effectively exact for the electronic problem at any reasonable cost. With cc-pVTZ the basis-set incompleteness is small (well under 0.005 Å from CBS). Experimental r_e(H2) ≈ 0.7414 Å; CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ should land within ~0.001–0.002 Å of that. Total wall time will be seconds. Cheaper alternatives (B3LYP, HF) are listed below if the user prefers a DFT reference.
alternatives: HF / cc-pVTZ — fast, but gives ~0.734 Å (no correlation, ~0.007 Å too short).
B3LYP-D3(BJ) / def2-TZVP — typical organic-DFT default; gives ~0.743 Å.
CCSD(T) / cc-pVQZ — closer to CBS limit, marginal improvement (<0.001 Å) for slightly more cost.
arguments.tradeoffs: CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ on H2 is sub-second; no meaningful cost penalty over HF here.

arguments.summary:
Computed the equilibrium H–H bond length of H2 at the CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ level (user-accepted recommendation). Starting from an RDKit-embedded geometry (initial r = 0.708 Å), psi4's optimizer converged in 0 iterations after the initial gradient evaluation, placing the two H atoms at x = ±0.371317 Å along the bond axis.

**Equilibrium bond length: r_e(H–H) = 0.7426 Å** (2 × 0.371317467752 Å), with final electronic energy E = −1.172336 Hartree. This agrees with the experimental r_e(H2) = 0.7414 Å to within 0.0013 Å, which is the expected accuracy of CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ — essentially the basis-set incompleteness error (CCSD(T) is exact for a two-electron system). Since H2 is a diatomic and the optimization converged to a bonded geometry, no frequency analysis was needed to confirm the minimum (the PES has a single well along r).
